sentences.text: [amused] He said, "We pay maybe eighty bucks in subscriptions." The bank said two hundred and nineteen.
He's not alone. In a survey of a thousand people, the average guess was eighty-six dollars a month. The real total was two hundred and nineteen.

visual.title: Survey of 1,000 people: subscriptions a month
visual.source: C+R Research survey of 1,000 US adults, 2022

sentences.text: Streaming, apps, the gym, cloud storage, the kids' games. Each one is small, so none of them feel like a bill.
[thoughtful] And here's the expensive part. That hundred and thirty-three dollars gets spent twice: once on the subscriptions, and again because you thought it was still there.
DivvyUpp finds them in your bank history and counts them with your bills, automatically.
Then savings goes first, and what's left becomes one number for today, after every subscription has been taken out.
[warm] So, eighty or two-nineteen? Your statement knows. Save first. Then spend what's safe. Try it at Divvyup dot com.
